int_reach_out.title: Talk to someone you trust
steps: Think of someone you feel comfortable with: someone on the team, someone at home or the psychological support service
Tell them how you have been feeling lately, without needing to go into detail
If you would rather do it privately, use “I need to talk”: it goes through a confidential channel
If the discomfort lasts for several days, ask for professional support

int_box_breathing.title: Box breathing
steps: Sit comfortably and relax your shoulders
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds
Hold your breath for 4 seconds
Exhale through your mouth for 4 seconds
Hold your lungs empty for 4 seconds
Repeat for 4 cycles

int_cbt_reframe.title: Reframing thoughts (brief CBT)
steps: Write down the situation that worries you in one sentence
Note the automatic thought that comes to mind (“everything is going to go wrong”)
Look for evidence for and against that thought
Write down a more balanced alternative
Rate from 1 to 5 how you feel before and after

int_journal.title: 5-minute journal
steps: Write down three things that went well today, however small
Note one thing you found hard and how you handled it
Write down something you would like to do tomorrow
The journal stays on this device: it is not shared

int_connect_crew.title: Time with the team or with family
steps: Suggest a shared activity: a meal, a game or a film
Or record a message for someone at home
Share something about your day, even briefly
When you finish, do your check-in and compare how you feel

int_sleep_light.title: Sleep hygiene and light
steps: Keep the same bedtime and wake-up time
Get bright light in the morning and dim light in the last hour of the day
Put screens away 30 minutes before bed
Avoid caffeine in the 6 hours before going to bed
Try to sleep at least 7 hours

int_movement_break.title: Active break
steps: Stand up and stretch your neck, shoulders and back
Do 5 minutes of gentle exercise: squats, lunges or cycling
Finish with three slow breaths
Note your energy level before and after

int_exercise_session.title: Resistance exercise session
steps: Warm up for 5 minutes
Do resistance exercises for your legs, hips and back
Add some cardio (treadmill, bike or walking)
Log your exercise minutes when you finish

int_bp_out_of_range.title: Blood pressure out of range: what to do while you wait for a response
steps: Stop what you are doing and sit down with your back supported
Breathe slowly for 5 minutes, without talking
Measure again with your arm at heart level and log the value
If you notice chest pain, shortness of breath, blurred vision, weakness or difficulty speaking, call for emergency help now with the SOS button
Do not take any new medication unless the medical officer tells you to
If it stays out of range, measure again every 15 minutes and do not stay alone

med_breath_awareness.title: Mindful breathing
steps: Sit or lie down comfortably and let your body rest
Close your eyes or look at a fixed point for 10 seconds
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 seconds
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 seconds
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 seconds
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 seconds
Breathe at your own pace and notice the air coming in and out for 60 seconds
Slowly open your eyes when you are ready

med_sounds.title: Focus on sounds
steps: Choose a soundscape, get comfortable and close your eyes
Listen to the sound without judging it for 60 seconds
If your mind wanders, gently come back to the sound for 60 seconds
Notice the sound and your breathing at the same time for 60 seconds
Let the sound fade into the background and rest for 30 seconds
Slowly open your eyes when you are ready

med_body_scan.title: Body scan
steps: Lie down or sit comfortably and close your eyes
Bring your attention to your feet and notice how they feel for 30 seconds
Move up to your legs and release any tension you find for 30 seconds
Notice your belly and your back as you breathe for 40 seconds
Bring your attention to your chest and your breathing for 40 seconds
Relax your shoulders, arms and hands for 40 seconds
Relax your neck, jaw and face for 40 seconds
Feel your whole body at once, calm and supported, for 60 seconds
Slowly move your fingers and open your eyes when you are ready

med_pmr.title: Progressive muscle relaxation
steps: Sit comfortably with your back supported
Clench your fists tightly for 5 seconds
Let go all at once and notice the difference for 15 seconds
Raise your shoulders towards your ears for 5 seconds
Release them and let them drop for 15 seconds
Scrunch up your face and squeeze your eyes shut for 5 seconds
Let go and relax your forehead and jaw for 15 seconds
Tense your legs and point your toes for 5 seconds
Let go and let your legs feel heavy for 15 seconds
Breathe calmly and notice your whole body relaxed for 60 seconds

med_sleep.title: Before bed
steps: If you are going to sleep, select “Sleep” in Activity and lie down
Dim the lights and close your eyes for 10 seconds
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale very slowly for 8 seconds
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale very slowly for 8 seconds
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale very slowly for 8 seconds
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 seconds
Exhale very slowly for 8 seconds
Go over your day without judging it and let it go for 60 seconds
Notice how heavy your body feels on the bed for 60 seconds
Let the sound keep you company: there is nothing else you need to do
